outlooks.summary: SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS WILL BE POSSIBLE TODAY AND TONIGHT FROM PORTIONS OF THE SOUTHERN AND CENTRAL GREAT PLAINS NORTHEASTWARD TO THE UPPER MISSISSIPPI VALLEY. THE GREATEST POTENTIAL FOR SEVERE STORMS WILL EXTEND FROM PORTIONS OF EASTERN KANSAS INTO SOUTHERN IOWA...WHERE LARGE HAIL...DAMAGING WINDS...AND A COUPLE OF TORNADOES WILL BE POSSIBLE.

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: A MIDLEVEL TROUGH AND ACCOMPANYING SPEED MAX ARE FORECAST TO PROGRESS FROM PORTIONS OF THE CNTRL GREAT BASIN AND CNTRL ROCKIES TO THE UPPER MS VALLEY THROUGH THE PERIOD. AS THIS OCCURS...SFC LOW PRESSURE WILL DEVELOP NEWD ALONG A FRONTAL ZONE FROM PORTIONS OF THE CNTRL GREAT PLAINS TO LAKE SUPERIOR. A COLD FRONT TRAILING SWWD FROM THE LOW WILL SURGE SWD...OVERTAKING A PREFRONTAL TROUGH/DRYLINE. THE PREFRONTAL TROUGH/DRYLINE SHOULD EXTEND SWWD FROM CNTRL KS TO THE SRN HIGH PLAINS AROUND PEAK HEATING. TO THE SE...HURRICANE MATTHEW IS FORECAST TO APPROACH THE EAST FLORIDA COAST DURING THE PERIOD.

sections.title: PORTIONS OF ERN KS AND SERN NEB EWD ACROSS IA AND NRN/WRN MO
sections.text: ELEVATED CONVECTION WILL LIKELY BE ONGOING AT THE BEGINNING OF THE FORECAST PERIOD FROM ERN PORTIONS OF THE CNTRL PLAINS...SPREADING NEWD TO THE UPPER MS VALLEY. THIS ACTIVITY WILL BE ASSOCIATED WITH ISENTROPIC ASCENT ALONG A SSWLY LLJ FORECAST TO LINGER THROUGH THE PERIOD. THIS ACTIVITY SHOULD PERSIST ACROSS PARTS OF THE MID MO VALLEY AND VICINITY INTO THE AFTERNOON...AS THE AFOREMENTIONED SFC LOW DEVELOPS NEWD...AND THE LLJ BECOMES FOCUSED FROM ERN KS AND SERN NEB INTO NRN MO AND IA. AN ASSOCIATED PRECIP-REINFORCED BOUNDARY WILL LIKELY EXTEND APPROXIMATELY W-E FROM PARTS OF ERN NEB INTO IA...TO THE S OF THE PRIMARY SYNOPTIC WARM FRONT. THIS SRN BOUNDARY SHOULD EDGE NWD IN RESPONSE TO POLEWARD MASS FLUXES ACCOMPANYING THE LLJ. AT LEAST MODEST DIURNAL HEATING OF THE MOIST BOUNDARY LAYER S OF THE PRECIP-REINFORCED BOUNDARY -- E.G. SFC DEWPOINTS IN THE MIDDLE/UPPER 60S -- WILL ALLOW MLCAPE TO INCREASE TO 1500-2500 J/KG TO THE E OF THE PRE-FRONTAL TROUGH/OVERTAKING COLD FRONT. CONVECTION WILL LIKELY INTENSIFY BY AFTERNOON ALONG THIS TROUGH...AND IN THE DOWNSHEAR WAA PATTERN. THE PRESENCE OF 40-50 KT OF DEEP SHEAR...WITH MIDLEVEL FLOW VECTORS OBLIQUELY CROSSING THE PRE-FRONTAL TROUGH..

sections.title: PORTIONS OF SRN KS SWWD INTO NW TX AND THE ERN TX PANHANDLE
sections.text: TSTMS WILL LIKELY DEVELOP BY MID/LATE AFTERNOON ALONG THE PRE-FRONTAL TROUGH/DRYLINE...AS LOW-LEVEL LAPSE RATES STEEPEN -- PARTICULARLY TO THE W OF THESE BOUNDARIES. THIS REGION WILL BE REMOVED FROM THE STRONGEST MIDLEVEL FLOW ACCOMPANYING THE SPEED MAX. HOWEVER...THE PRESENCE OF 30-40-KT SWLYS/WSWLYS AT H5 SHOULD OFFER SUFFICIENT DEEP SHEAR FOR MULTICELL CLUSTERS -- PERHAPS A FEW INITIAL SUPERCELL STRUCTURES -- TO SPREAD EWD/SEWD. AS THE COLD FRONT OVERTAKES THIS CONVECTION...UPSCALE GROWTH INTO SEWD-MOVING QUASI-LINEAR SEGMENTS MAY OCCUR THROUGH THE EVENING AND INTO THE OVERNIGHT HOURS. WITH AMPLE LOW-LEVEL MOISTURE IN PLACE ACROSS THE SRN GREAT PLAINS -- REF. 00Z OUN RAOB SAMPLING A 14.3-G/KG MEAN MIXING RATIO IN THE LOWEST 100 MB -- MLCAPE AROUND 2000-3000 J/KG SHOULD SUPPORT VIGOROUS UPDRAFTS CAPABLE OF ISOLATED TO WIDELY SCATTERED SVR WIND/HAIL. THIS RISK WILL PEAK BY LATE AFTERNOON/EARLY EVENING...AND GRADUALLY LESSEN AS CONVECTION SPREADS SEWD OVERNIGHT. FORECAST SOUNDINGS SUGGEST THAT SUFFICIENT LOW-LEVEL DIRECTIONAL SHEAR SHOULD EXIST FROM S-CNTRL KS INTO N-CNTRL OK FOR A LOW POTENTIAL OF A TORNADO WITH INCIPIENT SUPERCELL STRUCTURES.

sections.title: PORTIONS OF SRN/CNTRL WI
sections.text: PERSISTENT WAA THROUGH THE PERIOD WILL LIKELY SUPPORT MULTIPLE ROUNDS OF CONVECTION THROUGH THE PERIOD. STRENGTHENING LOW/MID-LEVEL FLOW -- ESPECIALLY LATE -- MAY SUPPORT A FEW TSTMS CAPABLE OF PRODUCING MARGINALLY SVR HAIL/WIND. HOWEVER...WITH THE MIDLEVEL SPEED MAX LAGGING WELL TO THE W OF THE REGION AT PEAK HEATING...AND GIVEN GENERALLY POOR LOW/MID-LEVEL LAPSE RATES...CONFIDENCE IN A GREATER SVR RISK IS TOO LIMITED FOR MORE THAN MRGL SVR PROBABILITIES AT THIS TIME.

sections.title: IMMEDIATE COASTAL SECTIONS OF THE ERN FL PENINSULA
sections.text: THE LATEST FORECAST FROM THE NATIONAL HURRICANE CENTER SUGGESTS THAT THE FAVORABLE NE QUADRANT OF HURRICANE MATTHEW -- WHERE MAXIMIZATION OF SUFFICIENT BUOYANCY/SRH EXISTS -- SHOULD REMAIN OFFSHORE DURING THE PERIOD. AMPLE LOW-LEVEL SRH WILL LIKELY GLANCE THE COASTAL AREAS...AND THERE IS SOME POTENTIAL FOR ROTATING CELLS IN FEEDER BANDS AND PERIPHERAL TO THE CENTER OF MATTHEW TO APPROACH THE COAST. HOWEVER...ANY TORNADO POTENTIAL WILL BE HIGHLY CONDITIONAL UPON SUFFICIENTLY STEEP LOW-LEVEL LAPSE RATES BEING SHUNTED INLAND. PRESENT INDICATIONS ARE THAT THIS WILL BE UNLIKELY GIVEN THE FORECAST TRACK OF MATTHEW. THIS WOULD ESPECIALLY BE THE CASE GIVEN ABUNDANT THETA-E DEFICITS ENCOURAGED BY WIDESPREAD MAINLAND PRECIPITATION RELATED TO MATTHEW. NEVERTHELESS...THE RISK FOR A BRIEF TORNADO MAY NOT BE ENTIRELY NEGLIGIBLE ALONG THE IMMEDIATE E COAST OF FLORIDA -- ESPECIALLY BY LATE IN THE PERIOD. ..COHEN/MOSIER.. 10/06/2016

outlooks.summary: SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS WILL BE POSSIBLE THIS AFTERNOON AND TONIGHT FROM THE SOUTH-CENTRAL GREAT PLAINS NORTHEASTWARD TO THE UPPER MISSISSIPPI VALLEY. THE GREATEST POTENTIAL FOR SEVERE STORMS WILL EXTEND FROM PORTIONS OF EASTERN KANSAS INTO SOUTHERN IOWA...WHERE LARGE HAIL...DAMAGING WINDS...AND A COUPLE OF TORNADOES WILL BE POSSIBLE.

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: AS AN UPPER LOW CONTINUES TO MOVE SLOWLY OVER THE CANADIAN PRAIRIES...A BASE-EMBEDDED SHORTWAVE TROUGH/SPEED MAX READILY EVIDENT OVER THE CENTRAL ROCKIES EARLY THIS MORNING WILL SPREAD EAST-NORTHEASTWARD AND REACH THE MIDDLE MO VALLEY/UPPER MIDWEST TONIGHT. IN RESPONSE...SURFACE LOW PRESSURE ACROSS THE SOUTH-CENTRAL PLAINS WILL STEADILY SHIFT NORTHEASTWARD TOWARD NORTHEAST KS/SOUTHEAST NEB BY EARLY EVENING...WITH THE SURFACE LOW /AND COLD FRONT/ EVENTUALLY REACHING WI AND THE LAKE SUPERIOR VICINITY EARLY FRIDAY. LATER TODAY INTO TONIGHT...THE AFOREMENTIONED SHORTWAVE TROUGH/JET STREAK WILL INCREASINGLY INTERACT WITH A SEASONALLY MOIST AIR MASS /60S F SURFACE DEWPOINTS/ TO THE EAST OF A DRYLINE AND AHEAD OF AN EAST-SOUTHEAST-ADVANCING COLD FRONT ACROSS THE SOUTH-CENTRAL PLAINS INTO THE MIDDLE MO VALLEY.

sections.title: SOUTHERN/CENTRAL PLAINS TO MO VALLEY/UPPER MIDWEST
sections.text: A POINT OF UNCERTAINTY RELATES TO THE PERSISTENCE OF EXTENSIVE OVERNIGHT/EARLY-MORNING CONVECTION ACROSS SOUTHEAST KS/NORTHEAST OK...WITH CONVECTIVE OVERTURNING AND AN OBSERVED 5-10F DRYING OF SURFACE DEWPOINTS IN SOME AREAS OVERNIGHT. EVEN WHILE MOIST ADVECTION WILL BE STRONG TODAY AND THIS CONVECTION SHOULD GRADUALLY DECAY THIS MORNING...IT NONETHELESS CASTS SOME UNCERTAINTY REGARDING THE AIR MASS/BOUNDARY-LAYER QUALITY WITH NORTH/NORTHEASTWARD EXTENT LATER TODAY INTO PARTS OF IA/MO/EASTERN NEB. ACCORDINGLY...THE STRONGEST DESTABILIZATION BY MID/LATE AFTERNOON WILL BE ACROSS EAST-CENTRAL/SOUTHEAST KS SOUTH-SOUTHWESTWARD INTO WESTERN/CENTRAL OK AND WESTERN NORTH TX TODAY AHEAD OF THE COLD FRONT/DRY LINE...WHERE AMPLE BUOYANCY WITH 3000+ J/KG IS POSSIBLE BY PEAK HEATING. ALTHOUGH NOT AS ROBUSTLY UNSTABLE AS FARTHER SOUTH...SEVERE-CONDUCIVE MOISTENING/DESTABILIZATION SHOULD OCCUR INTO NORTHEAST KS/SOUTHEAST NEB AND EVEN ADJACENT PARTS OF IA/MO BY LATE AFTERNOON AND EVENING...PARTICULARLY GIVEN THAT THE STRONGEST DPVA/FORCING FOR ASCENT AND DEEP-LAYER SHEAR WILL BE FOCUSED INTO THESE REGIONS BY LATE AFTERNOON INTO TONIGHT. AS STRONGER ASCENT APPROACHES THE REGION...SOME ELEVATED STRO

sections.title: EASTERN FL PENINSULA
sections.text: THE LATEST FORECAST FROM THE NATIONAL HURRICANE CENTER SUGGESTS THAT THE TORNADO-FAVORABLE NORTHEAST QUADRANT OF HURRICANE MATTHEW -- WHERE SUFFICIENT BUOYANCY/SRH WILL BE MAXIMIZED -- SHOULD REMAIN FOCUSED OFFSHORE DURING THE PERIOD. EVEN SO...AS THE CENTER OF MATTHEW POTENTIALLY APPROACHES COASTAL EASTERN FL THIS EVENING/OVERNIGHT...AMPLE LOW-LEVEL SRH WILL LIKELY GLANCE EASTERN COASTAL AREAS. ACCORDINGLY...THERE IS SOME POTENTIAL FOR ROTATING CELLS IN FEEDER BANDS AND PERIPHERAL TO THE CENTER OF MATTHEW TO APPROACH THE COAST...WITH AT LEAST SOME POTENTIAL FOR A BRIEF TORNADO OR TWO...MAINLY FOR IMMEDIATE COASTAL AREAS OF THE EASTERN FL PENINSULA TONIGHT/EARLY FRIDAY. ..GUYER/COOK.. 10/06/2016

outlooks.summary: SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS APPEAR LIKELY THIS AFTERNOON AND EVENING ACROSS PARTS OF THE CENTRAL PLAINS AND ADJACENT MID MISSOURI VALLEY...PARTICULARLY ACROSS PARTS OF NORTHEASTERN KANSAS AND SOUTHEASTERN NEBRASKA INTO SOUTHWESTERN IOWA AND NORTHWESTERN MISSOURI.

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: A SIGNIFICANT SHORT WAVE IMPULSE...WITHIN LARGER-SCALE UPPER TROUGHING IN THE MID-LATITUDE WESTERLIES...IS IN THE PROCESS OF ACCELERATING NORTHEASTWARD OUT OF THE EASTERN GREAT BASIN/CENTRAL ROCKIES REGION. MODELS INDICATE THAT THIS FEATURE WILL ADVANCE ACROSS THE NORTH CENTRAL PLAINS AND MID MISSOURI VALLEY LATER TODAY AND TONIGHT. AS IT DOES...IT MAY COME INCREASINGLY IN PHASE WITH AN IMPULSE PIVOTING AROUND THE SOUTHERN PERIPHERY OF A CYCLONIC CIRCULATION NOW CENTERED NEAR THE SOUTHERN SASKATCHEWAN/MANITOBA BORDER AREA. ASSOCIATED FORCING FOR ASCENT MAY CONTRIBUTE TO SURFACE CYCLOGENESIS ACROSS PARTS OF THE UPPER MIDWEST AND UPPER GREAT LAKES REGION BY LATE TONIGHT...WITH A TRAILING SURFACE COLD FRONT FORECAST TO SURGE SOUTH OF THE UPPER MISSISSIPPI/MID MISSOURI VALLEY AND CENTRAL PLAINS THROUGH MUCH OF THE SOUTH CENTRAL PLAINS AND MID MISSOURI VALLEY BY 12Z FRIDAY. WELL SOUTH OF THE STRONGER WESTERLIES...MAJOR HURRICANE MATTHEW IS EXPECTED TO GRADUALLY MIGRATE INTO...AND NORTHWARD ALONG...THE FLORIDA ATLANTIC COAST LATER TODAY THROUGH TONIGHT.

sections.title: CENTRAL PLAINS...MID/LOWER MISSOURI VALLEY REGION
sections.text: A PERSISTENT AREA OF THUNDERSTORM ACTIVITY AND ASSOCIATED CLOUD COVER ACROSS PARTS OF THE LOWER CENTRAL PLAINS INTO LOWER MISSOURI VALLEY PROBABLY WILL CONTINUE TO SLOWLY WEAKEN/DIMINISH THROUGH THE DAY. BUT THIS MAY NOT BE IN TIME TO ALLOW FOR SUBSTANTIVE BOUNDARY LAYER DESTABILIZATION ACROSS AREAS CURRENTLY IMPACTED PRIOR TO COLD FRONTAL PASSAGE THIS EVENING. HOWEVER...IN THE WAKE OF THE ONGOING ACTIVITY...AT LEAST A NARROW CORRIDOR OF SUBSTANTIVE DESTABILIZATION APPEARS POSSIBLE ALONG THE QUASI-STATIONARY FRONTAL ZONE NOW EXTENDING FROM NEAR/NORTH OF THE MISSOURI/IOWA BORDER INTO THE CENTRAL HIGH PLAINS. THIS FRONT WILL PROVIDE THE FOCUS FOR A NORTHEASTWARD MIGRATING SURFACE WAVE OUT OF SOUTHWEST KANSAS ACROSS THE MID MISSOURI VALLEY THROUGH THIS EVENING...BEFORE MORE SUBSTANTIVE SURFACE LOW DEVELOPMENT/DEEPENING TAKES PLACE LATER TONIGHT ACROSS THE UPPER MIDWEST/GREAT LAKES REGION. THE PRIMARY SEVERE WEATHER POTENTIAL FOR THIS PERIOD IS EXPECTED TO ACCOMPANY THE SURFACE WAVE AS IT TRACKS ACROSS PARTS OF NORTH CENTRAL/NORTHEAST KANSAS INTO THE MID MISSOURI VALLEY LATE THIS AFTERNOON. GIVEN MOISTURE NOW PRESENT IN THE WARM SECTOR...THE DEVELOPMENT OF MODERATELY LARGE CAPE /UP TO

sections.title: FLORIDA ATLANTIC COASTAL AREAS
sections.text: GIVEN THE PROXIMITY OF MAJOR HURRICANE MATTHEW TO THE FLORIDA ATLANTIC COAST...AND SOME LINGERING UNCERTAINTY CONCERNING THE EXACT TRACK...THE DEVELOPMENT OF A RISK FOR ISOLATED TORNADOES IS NOT OUT OF THE QUESTION TONIGHT. HOWEVER...BASED ON THE CURRENT FORECAST TRACK...THE POTENTIAL FOR APPRECIABLE INLAND BOUNDARY LAYER DESTABILIZATION ALLOWING FOR TORNADIC POTENTIAL STILL SEEMS LOW AT THE PRESENT TIME. ..KERR/PICCA.. 10/06/2016

outlooks.summary: SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ARE LIKELY THIS AFTERNOON AND EVENING ACROSS PARTS OF THE CENTRAL PLAINS AND ADJACENT MID MISSOURI VALLEY...PARTICULARLY ACROSS PARTS OF EASTERN KANSAS AND SOUTHEASTERN NEBRASKA INTO SOUTHWESTERN IOWA AND NORTHWESTERN MISSOURI. ISOLATED TORNADOES...ONE OR TWO OF WHICH MAY BE STRONG...LARGE TO VERY LARGE HAIL...AND DAMAGING WINDS WILL ALL BE POSSIBLE.

sections.title: 20Z UPDATE
sections.text: PRIMARY CHANGE WITH THIS UPDATE IS TO INCREASE TORNADO PROBABILITIES ACROSS PARTS OF SERN NEB AND FAR NWRN MO INTO ERN KS. A STRONG TORNADO OR TWO MAY ALSO OCCUR ACROSS THIS REGION. LATEST SFC OBSERVATIONS AND VISIBLE SATELLITE IMAGERY SHOW AN INCREASINGLY MOIST AND UNSTABLE LOW-LEVEL AIRMASS AS DIURNAL HEATING BECOMES MAXIMIZED. A WARM FRONT EXTENDS ACROSS NERN KS/SERN NEB NEWD INTO S-CNTRL IA...AND AN OUTFLOW BOUNDARY FROM PRIOR CONVECTION IS LOCATED FROM NERN OK INTO S-CNTRL KS. EFFECTIVE SRH VALUES WILL LIKELY BE ENHANCED ALONG THESE BOUNDARIES THROUGH THE EARLY EVENING HOURS WHERE SFC WINDS ARE BACKED TO SLY/SELY. SHEAR VECTORS NEARLY ORTHOGONAL TO THE BOUNDARY ACROSS CNTRL/ERN KS SHOULD FAVOR AN INITIAL SUPERCELL MODE FOR AT LEAST A FEW HOURS THIS AFTERNOON... BEFORE THE LINEAR FORCING OF THE FRONT LIKELY ENCOURAGES UPSCALE GROWTH INTO A SQUALL LINE WITH DAMAGING WINDS BECOMING THE MAIN THREAT. THE 30 PERCENT WIND PROBABILITIES/ENH AREA HAVE ALSO BEEN EXPANDED SEWD INTO MORE OF ERN KS/WRN MO BASED ON LATEST SHORT-TERM MODEL GUIDANCE SUGGESTING A DAMAGING BOW MOVING THROUGH THIS REGION THROUGH THE EARLY EVENING. mesoscale_discussions.summary: A THREAT FOR ISOLATED SVR HAIL WILL ACCOMPANY ONGOING ELEVATED TSTMS OVER SERN NEB...FAR NERN KS...AND SWRN IA. WATCH ISSUANCE IS NOT ANTICIPATED IN THE NEAR-TERM...BUT WILL BECOME MORE PROBABLE THIS AFTERNOON AS THE POTENTIAL FOR ALL SVR HAZARDS INCREASES.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: SCATTERED ELEVATED TSTMS HAVE DEVELOPED N OF A WARM FRONT INTO SERN NEB. WHILE RECENT RADAR TRENDS SUGGEST THIS ACTIVITY IS MOSTLY SUB-SEVERE...A GRADUAL INCREASE IN INTENSITY CONTINUES TO OCCUR. A GRADUAL NWD MOVEMENT OF THE WARM FRONT INTO SERN NEB IS OCCURRING AS POCKETS OF STRONGER HEATING ARE NOTED ACROSS NERN KS...AND THIS IS SUPPORTING MORE SUBSTANTIAL DESTABILIZATION NWD. THE PRIMARY SHORT-TERM THREAT ASSOCIATED WITH ONGOING ACTIVITY APPEARS TO BE LARGE HAIL AMIDST STEEP MID-LEVEL LAPSE RATES BUT A COOL BOUNDARY LAYER. ADDITIONAL TSTM DEVELOPMENT LATER THIS AFTERNOON IS LIKELY FROM A TRIPLE POINT OVER CNTRL KS NEWD INTO SERN NEB AND SWRN IA ALONG A WARM FRONT...WHERE THE POTENTIAL FOR SUPERCELLS CAPABLE OF ALL SEVERE HAZARDS MAY EXIST. WHILE NEAR-TERM CONVECTIVE TRENDS ARE MORE UNCERTAIN FOR IMMEDIATE WATCH ISSUANCE...THE CURRENT FORECAST FOR INCREASING SVR POTENTIAL INTO THE AFTERNOON MAKES WATCH ISSUANCE MORE LIKELY AFTER 18Z.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THE POTENTIAL FOR ALL SVR HAZARDS WILL INCREASE THIS AFTERNOON FROM CNTRL KS INTO PARTS OF WRN IA. RAPID TSTM DEVELOPMENT IS EXPECTED ALONG A COLD FRONT THIS AFTERNOON...AND A TORNADO WATCH WILL LIKELY BE ISSUED BY 20Z.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A SHORTWAVE IMPULSE OVER THE CNTRL HIGH PLAINS WILL ACCELERATE NEWD THIS AFTERNOON AND EVENING...AND WILL SUPPORT AN EWD COLD FRONTAL SURGE ACROSS WRN/CNTRL PORTIONS OF KS/NEB AS A SFC LOW BECOMES REPOSITIONED TOWARDS THE MID-MO VALLEY THIS EVENING. FORCING FOR ASCENT ASSOCIATED WITH THE COLD FRONT AND SHORTWAVE IMPULSE...ALONG WITH ADDITIONAL HEATING LEADING TO A WEAKENING OF CINH...IS EXPECTED TO RESULT IN A RAPID INCREASE IN TSTM COVERAGE THROUGH THE LATE AFTERNOON FROM SRN NEB INTO CNTRL KS. OTHER TSTMS WILL PERSIST/DEVELOP ALONG A WARM FRONT EXTENDING ACROSS FAR SERN NEB INTO CNTRL IA...AS A 30-40 KT LLJ REMAINS FOCUSED ACROSS THIS AREA. ONE POTENTIAL AREA OF IMMEDIATE CONCERN IS ASSOCIATED WITH A TSTM MOVING INTO SWRN IA /AS OF 1820Z/ AND TRACKING CLOSE TO THE WARM FRONT...WHILE THE AIR MASS DESTABILIZES ACROSS WRN/CNTRL IA. THE BIGGEST UNCERTAINTY THROUGHOUT THE MORNING AND EARLY AFTERNOON HAS CENTERED AROUND THE DEGREE OF DESTABILIZATION THAT CAN OCCUR...BUT VISIBLE SATELLITE TRENDS REVEAL MORE WIDESPREAD CLEARING ACROSS NERN KS INTO SWRN IA AMIDST A THINNING CIRRUS FIELD. MLCAPE VALUES RANGING FROM 500-1000 J/KG ACROSS IA TO 2000-3000 J/KG ACROSS CNTRL KS ARE EXPECTED TO BECOME ESTABLISHED AROUND THE TIME OF MORE WIDESPREAD CONVECTIVE DEVELOPMENT. STRONG LOW-MIDLEVEL WIND PROFILES WILL FAVOR THE POTENTIAL FOR A FEW SUPERCELLS TO DEVELOP. AN ASSOCIATED TORNADO THREAT IS EXPECTED TO REMAIN GREATEST ALONG THE WARM FRONT...AND PERHAPS ASSOCIATED WITH ANY DISCRETE TSTMS THAT INITIALLY DEVELOP ALONG THE COLD FRONT INTO CNTRL KS. THE INCREASING LOW-LEVEL FORCING FOR ASCENT ALONG THE COLD FRONT SHOULD EVENTUALLY RESULT IN UPSCALE GROWTH INTO A MCS THIS EVENING...WITH A DMGG WIND THREAT EXPECTED TO EVENTUALLY BECOME DOMINANT.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THUNDERSTORMS ARE EXPECTED TO DEVELOP THIS AFTERNOON ACROSS PORTIONS OF WESTERN AND NORTHERN OKLAHOMA...AS WELL AS FAR NORTHWEST TEXAS. THE PRIMARY THREATS WILL BE LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WINDS...WITH THE POTENTIAL FOR A TORNADO OR TWO AS WELL...MOST LIKELY ACROSS NORTH-CENTRAL OKLAHOMA. WATCH ISSUANCE IS LIKELY WITHIN THE NEXT 2-3 HOURS.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: THE LATEST VISIBLE SATELLITE AND SFC OBSERVATIONS DEPICT A DRY LINE EXTENDING FROM SOUTHERN KS TO THE SOUTH/SOUTHWEST ACROSS FAR NORTHWEST OK AND INTO THE TX PANHANDLE. ADDITIONALLY...AN OUTFLOW BOUNDARY FROM PRIOR CONVECTION STRETCHES FROM JUST NORTH OF TULSA TO THE WEST AND NORTHWEST...REACHING SOUTH-CENTRAL KS. BETWEEN THESE TWO BOUNDARIES...CONTINUED INSOLATION AND RICH BOUNDARY-LAYER MOISTURE ARE YIELDING AMPLE BUOYANCY...CHARACTERIZED BY AROUND 2000-3000 J/KG OF MLCAPE. WHILE SFC CONVERGENCE IS NOT PARTICULARLY STRONG...MODEST FORCING FOR ASCENT ON THE SOUTHEASTERN PERIPHERY OF A WESTERN US TROUGH SHOULD LEAD TO SCATTERED THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT LATER THIS AFTERNOON. SOME OF THESE INITIAL CELLS MAY GAIN SUPERCELLULAR CHARACTERISTICS...AIDED BY EFFECTIVE SHEAR OF 30-40 KTS...ESPECIALLY ACROSS NORTHERN OKLAHOMA. IN ADDITION TO UPDRAFT ORGANIZATION/ROTATION...RELATIVELY STEEP LAPSE RATES ALOFT WILL SUPPORT LARGE HAIL IN DISCRETE CONVECTION. A TORNADO OR TWO MAY ALSO BE POSSIBLE...PRIMARILY ACROSS FAR NORTH-CENTRAL OK...WHERE SFC FLOW WILL BE SLIGHTLY BACKED CLOSER TO THE AFOREMENTIONED OUTFLOW BOUNDARY. THROUGH THE LATE AFTERNOON AND EVENING HOURS HOWEVER...LINEAR FORCING ALONG THE DRY LINE AND A SOUTHWARD-SURGING COLD FRONT WILL LIKELY FORCE THE SEVERE THREAT TO TRANSITION TO PRIMARILY STRONG WIND. MOREOVER...THE MID-LEVEL WIND PROFILE WILL LIKELY ENCOURAGE CELL SPLITS...AS WELL AS A SIGNIFICANT COMPONENT OF CELL MOTION ALONG THE INITIATING BOUNDARIES. SUCH UPSCALE GROWTH WILL ALSO AID A TRANSITION TO LINE SEGMENTS WITH AN ATTENDANT WIND THREAT. REGARDLESS...THE EXPECTED STORM COVERAGE AND FAVORABLE THERMODYNAMIC ENVIRONMENT SUGGEST AN APPRECIABLE SEVERE THREAT SHOULD EMERGE OVER THE NEXT FEW HOURS. AS SUCH...WATCH ISSUANCE IS LIKELY BY MID/LATE AFTERNOON.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THREAT FOR TORNADOES INCLUDING POTENTIAL FOR STRONG TORNADOES WILL REMAIN GREATEST ACROSS PORTIONS OF ERN KS THROUGH 00Z. THE OVERALL THREAT SHOULD TRANSITION TO DAMAGING WIND TOWARD MID EVENING...BUT SOME TORNADO THREAT MAY PERSIST BEYOND 02Z.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: EARLY THIS EVENING A LINE OF SUPERCELLS CONTINUES DEVELOPING ALONG DRYLINE FROM NERN THROUGH SCNTRL KS. A NARROW CORRIDOR OF STRONG INSTABILITY RESIDES DOWNSTREAM FROM THE STORMS WHERE 50 KT EFFECTIVE BULK SHEAR AND 300-400 M2/S2 STORM-RELATIVE HELICITY EXISTS IN WARM SECTOR AND IN VICINITY OF A MODIFIED CONVECTIVE OUTFLOW BOUNDARY. THREAT FOR TORNADOES AND VERY LARGE HAIL WILL REMAIN GREATEST AS STORMS EVOLVE WITHIN THIS ENVIRONMENT NEXT COUPLE HOURS AND WHILE UPDRAFTS REMAIN AT LEAST PARTIALLY DISCRETE. HOWEVER...A COLD FRONT IS SURGING EWD AND MERGING WITH THE DRYLINE...AND THIS PROCESS MAY CONTRIBUTE TO AN EVENTUAL UPSCALE LINEAR GROWTH SUPPORTING AN INCREASE IN DAMAGING WIND THREAT BY 01Z. OTHER STORMS PERSIST ACROSS SERN KS. THESE STORMS HAVE EVOLVED INTO A CLUSTER. HOWEVER...THEY REMAIN IN AN ENVIRONMENT SUPPORTIVE OF EMBEDDED SUPERCELLS AND LOW-LEVEL MESOCYCLONES. DAMAGING WIND AND A FEW TORNADOES WILL REMAIN POSSIBLE WITH THIS ACTIVITY THROUGH 00Z. ..DIAL.. 10/06/2016 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: WIDELY SCATTERED THUNDERSTORMS DEVELOPING ALONG THE DRYLINE MAY POSE AN ISOLATED SEVERE HAIL AND DAMAGING WIND THREAT OVER THE NEXT COUPLE OF HOURS. GIVEN THE MARGINALITY OF THE SEVERE THREAT...A WW IS UNLIKELY.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: ISOLATED TO WIDELY SCATTERED THUNDERSTORMS HAVE DEVELOPED IN THE VICINITY OF THE DRYLINE ACROSS WESTERN TEXAS...WHERE STRONG INSOLATION HAS RESULTED IN DEEP VERTICAL MIXING AND CONVECTIVE INITIATION. WHILE MLCAPE VALUES EXCEED 2000 J/KG /PER MESOANALYSIS/ ACROSS MUCH OF THIS AREA...MARGINAL DEEP-LAYER SHEAR WILL LIMIT STORM ORGANIZATION AND LONGEVITY. THE STORMS WITH THE STRONGEST UPDRAFTS MAY POSE AN ISOLATED SEVERE HAIL AND WIND THREAT...BUT THE THREAT IS EXPECTED TO DIMINISH RAPIDLY AFTER SUNSET...PRECLUDING THE NEED FOR A WATCH.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THREAT FOR A TORNADO...DAMAGING WIND AND LARGE HAIL WILL SPREAD INTO A SMALL PART OF SWRN MO THIS EVENING. HOWEVER...AT THIS TIME IT APPEARS THREAT WILL PROBABLY REMAIN TOO LIMITED IN AREAL EXTENT FOR A WW.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: THIS EVENING A CLUSTER OF STORMS WITH A LEADING HP SUPERCELL IS MOVING THROUGH SERN KS. THESE STORMS WILL LIKELY CONTINUE INTO SWRN MO THIS EVENING. OBJECTIVE ANALYSIS SHOWS INSTABILITY BECOMES INCREASINGLY MARGINAL WITH EWD EXTENT INTO SWRN MO TO THE NORTH OF A CONVECTIVE OUTFLOW BOUNDARY WHERE THE SFC LAYER UNDERWENT ONLY PARTIAL RECOVERY. NEVERTHELESS...LOW-LEVEL HODOGRAPHS REMAIN LARGE AND EFFECTIVE BULK SHEAR FROM 40-50 KT WILL CONTINUE TO SUPPORT ORGANIZED STORM STRUCTURES WITH A THREAT FOR A TORNADO...DAMAGING WIND AND LARGE HAIL...AT LEAST INTO EXTREME SWRN MO NEXT COUPLE HOURS. HOWEVER...THE TENDENCY WILL BE FOR THE LLJ TO SHIFT NORTH OF THIS REGION WITH TIME...AND AS THE BOUNDARY LAYER CONTINUES TO COOL...FAVORABLE CONDITIONS FOR SEVERE STORMS WILL LIKELY ONLY REMAIN OVER A SMALL PORTION OF SWRN MO.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: CONVECTIVE MODE IS EXPECTED TO BECOME MORE LINEAR WITH TIME...ESPECIALLY ACROSS NORTHERN OKLAHOMA...AS THE COLD FRONT UNDERCUTS THE CONVECTION ALONG THE DRYLINE. THUS...THE THREAT FOR DAMAGING WINDS IS EXPECTED TO INCREASE INTO THE EVENING HOURS.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: DESPITE STORM SPLITS AND STORM INTERACTIONS ALONG THE DRYLINE...CONVECTIVE MODE TO THIS POINT HAS REMAINED RELATIVELY DISCRETE. HOWEVER...CONVECTION AHEAD OF THE COLD FRONT IN NORTHWESTERN OKLAHOMA IS BECOMING MUCH MORE LINEAR IN NATURE...AND THIS TRANSITION TO A LINEAR MODE IS EXPECTED TO CONTINUE ACROSS NORTHERN OKLAHOMA WITH AN INCREASING THREAT OF DAMAGING WINDS. FOR SOUTHWESTERN OKLAHOMA...CONVECTIVE MODE IS MORE UNCERTAIN THIS EVENING PRIOR TO FRONTAL PASSAGE...BUT INSTABILITY AND SHEAR SHOULD BE SUPPORTIVE OF AN EASTWARD-PROPAGATING CONVECTIVE CLUSTER CAPABLE OF PRODUCING SEVERE HAIL AND DAMAGING WIND. ..JIRAK.. 10/06/2016 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THIN SLIVER OF E-CENTRAL/NERN FL COASTAL AREA GENERALLY BETWEEN VRB-JAX WILL HAVE MRGL TORNADO RISK THROUGH REMAINDER OF EVENING INTO OVERNIGHT HOURS. POTENTIAL WILL SHIFT GRADUALLY NWD WITH TIME AND IN STEP WITH TRANSLATION OF TC. RISK IS TOO LOW AND CONDITIONAL TO WARRANT WW ATTM...BUT A BRIEF/WEAK TORNADO CANNOT BE ENTIRELY RULED OUT.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: BASED ON LATEST NHC FCST TRACK AND WIND FIELDS -- WHICH SERVE FOR THIS PURPOSE AS PROXY FOR STORM SIZE -- MOST FAVORABLE SECTOR OF HURRICANE MATTHEW FOR SUPERCELLS AND TORNADOES WILL REMAIN OFFSHORE WELL INTO TONIGHT. HOWEVER...WATERSPOUT MOVING ONSHORE OR SMALL/BRIEF SUPERCELL TORNADO MAY OCCUR WITH CELLS GENERALLY WEAKENING IN ORGANIZATION AS THEY MOVE ASHORE. VWP AND AVBL RAOBS SUGGEST ADEQUATE LOW-LEVEL SRH FOR ESPECIALLY WWD/RIGHT-MOVING CELLS TO ROTATE...HOWEVER MAIN LIMITING FACTOR WILL BE LACK OF MORE ROBUST BUOYANCY. MLCAPE DECREASES RAPIDLY WITH INLAND EXTENT FROM IMMEDIATE COAST...FROM OVER 1000 J/KG OFFSHORE TO AROUND 500 J/KG OR LESS INLAND. DIABATIC SFC COOLING WILL BE VERY SLOW/GRADUAL IN PRESENCE OF THETAE ADVECTION ONSHORE FROM ATLC...BUT WILL ACT TO DIMINISH INLAND CAPE EVEN FURTHER WITH TIME THROUGH TONIGHT. SECONDARY BUT STILL IMPORTANT FACTOR WILL BE CONVECTIVE MODE -- I.E. WHETHER ANY RELATIVELY DISCRETE/SUSTAINED SUPERCELLS OFFSHORE CAN SURVIVE VERY FAR MOVING RAPIDLY WWD/WSWWD INTO NWRN QUADRANT AIR MASS CHARACTERIZED BY BOTH MUCH LOWER CAPE AND MESSIER PRECIP STRUCTURES COMPARED TO OFFSHORE. GIVEN THESE CONDITIONALITIES... RISK IS NON-ZERO BUT TOO SMALL TO JUSTIFY WW ATTM. REF NHC ADVISORIES FOR LATEST FORECAST TRACK...INTENSITY...SURGE... TROPICAL WATCH...AND WARNING INFORMATION REGARDING MATTHEW. ..EDWARDS.. 10/07/2016 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: PRIMARY THREAT ACROSS ERN KS THROUGH WRN MO HAS TRANSITIONED TO ISOLATED DAMAGING WIND...BUT A QLCS TORNADO OR TWO CANNOT BE RULED OUT. TORNADO WATCH 493 WILL BE ALLOWED TO EXPIRE AT 02Z. DEPENDING ON CONVECTIVE TRENDS...A SEVERE THUNDERSTORM WATCH MIGHT BE NEEDED FOR A PORTION OF THIS REGION.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: STORMS WILL LIKELY CONTINUE DEVELOPING THROUGH ERN KS INTO WRN MO ALONG COLD FRONT AND WITHIN ZONE OF PRE-FRONTAL WARM ADVECTION. OTHER STORMS OVER SERN KS WILL LIKELY PERSIST THROUGH THE EVENING AS THEY SHIFT EWD INTO SWRN MO. CONVECTIVE MODE HAS TRANSITIONED TO MOSTLY LINEAR WITHIN AN ENVIRONMENT CHARACTERIZED BY STRONG VERTICAL SHEAR AND LARGE HODOGRAPHS...BUT INCREASINGLY MARGINAL INSTABILITY. THE BOUNDARY LAYER ACROSS MUCH OF WCNTRL THROUGH NWRN MO TO THE NORTH OF A LARGE REMNANT OUTFLOW BOUNDARY IS RELATIVELY STABLE...AND RECENT DEVELOPMENT OF WIDESPREAD SHOWERS AND STORMS WILL CONTINUE TO OVERTURN PRE-FRONTAL WARM SECTOR. THIS SUGGESTS NRN PORTION OF THE LINE WILL PROBABLY STRUGGLE AS IT MOVES THROUGH NERN KS AND NWRN MO. THE MOST FAVORABLE AREA FOR ADDITIONAL SEVERE STORMS MAY BE ACROSS SERN KS WHERE THE ATMOSPHERE IS MORE UNSTABLE SOUTH OF THE OUTFLOW BOUNDARY. ..DIAL.. 10/07/2016 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...
